liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (1 review): Listener describes the opening Bertha as rollicking but notes it doesn't go anywhere [14]
- **Next Time You See Me** (1 review): Listener identifies this as their favorite version, praising Jerry's singing and playing [7]
- **Loser** (1 review): Listener highlights Loser, Cumberland Blues, and Hard to Handle as standout moments [8]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Cumberland Blues stands out for having more intensity than usual [14]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Listener notes the China Cat Sunflower to I Know You Rider transition is real nice [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **microphone monitor level test!**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **car keys (genuine leather)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-04-22.167465.sbd.anon.gems.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 113 min [1]
- **gd71-04-22.sbd.clugston.2176.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 113 min; rated 3.93/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Listener notes the soundboard recording quality is nice and the music is tight; Listener describes the performance as solid, strong, and in the pocket; Listener praises the excellent sound from the spring of 1971 tour [4][6][11]

## Around the show

- Power cut threat shortened the show; listener sat on stage near Jerry [3]
- The band members were in a great mood with funny banter [4]
- Pigpen performed Hard to Handle, Good Lovin', and Next Time You See Me [6]
- Listener attended their only college-era show while studying at Colby in Waterville [9]
- Garcia was angry when power was cut, vowing they would never play Bangor again [10]
- The band would have played all night if venue rules allowed it [11]
- This was the Grateful Dead's first performance in Maine [1]
- This performance occurred just days before the Fillmore engagement [3]
- Show was slightly short and lacked Other One and Dark Star [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-04-22.167465.sbd.anon.gems.flac1644**: taped by Anon; transferred by DAT transferred and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Master soundboard reel > first generation reel > PCM > DAT (via Anon) [1]
- **gd71-04-22.sbd.clugston.2176.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Master Soundboard Reel transferred to DAT then CDR; shn encoded by Scott Clugston [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1971-04-22 GD NRPS Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1971-04-22-gd-nrps-poster/) [16]
- Fan art by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [April 22, 1971 Bangor Municipal Auditorium, Bangor, ME: Grateful Dead/NRPS (Northern Excursions)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2015/01/april-22-1971-bangor-municipal.html) [17]
- Fan art by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [April 22, 1971 Bangor Municipal Auditorium, Bangor, ME: Grateful Dead/NRPS (Northern Excursions)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2015/01/april-22-1971-bangor-municipal.html) [18]
